articles.title: Private Object Storage Uploads: User Documents with Signed Download URLs
articles.excerpt: A customer support app changes the storage decision the moment a 4 GB screen recording arrives. Proxying those bytes through a Node.js process consumes application connections, adds another failure bo…
articles.body: A customer support app changes the storage decision the moment a 4 GB screen recording arrives. Proxying those bytes through a Node.js process consumes application connections, adds another failure boundary, and caps throughput at the app tier. Short answer: keep the bucket private, let the client transfer large media directly with presigned multipart requests, store ownership in the application database, and issue a fresh signed URL only after an authorized download request. The app should control permission, not carry the payload. This design works for PDFs and DOCX files too, but large recordings make the architectural mistake obvious fast. Keep it private. The before-and-after throughput model Before: browser to app server to object storage.

articles.title: Your Claude Code sessions outlive the work. Who closes them?
articles.excerpt: Originally published at omerbinsaleem.com by Omer Bin Saleem (Omer Saleem). A usage report said most of my sessions had been open for more than eight hours. The fix was a small hourly job, and its fir…
articles.body: Originally published at omerbinsaleem.com by Omer Bin Saleem (Omer Saleem). A usage report said most of my sessions had been open for more than eight hours. The fix was a small hourly job, and its first version had a timezone bug that would have closed nothing. How to do it Read what /usage is telling you before guessing. Mine showed 94% of sessions asking for /clear and 65% open for 8 hours or more, with 10 sessions alive and 9 editor tabs between 15 and 17 hours old. Check the suspect before blaming it. I assumed Remote Control was keeping the tabs alive, but only 2 of the 5 old idle tabs had a bridge at all. The real cause was simpler: an editor tab keeps its process alive until the tab closes, and Claude Code never closes an idle session by itself. Make the reaper narrow on purpose.

articles.body: HAProxy client certificate checks stop at the chain and policy you configure Mutual TLS at a load balancer can look deceptively complete. HAProxy verifies a client certificate against a configured CA and accepts the TLS connection. The application behind the proxy may then receive an identity header or a certificate subject. The security result depends on what the proxy verified, what it forwarded, and whether the backend performs its own trust and authorization checks. HAProxy's client certificate tutorial shows verify required and ca-file on the frontend bind line. That configuration requires a client certificate and validates it against the named CA. It does not automatically map every valid certificate to an application role.

articles.body: When a requirement changes, the team needs to know what was approved, which work depends on it, and what may need to be reviewed or retested. If that information lives in disconnected documents and spreadsheets, change impact is easy to miss. A workable requirements process starts with a small, consistent data model and clear rules for review and traceability. Use a general project tool when your needs are lightweight and configurable; consider a specialist requirements or ALM system when formal baselines, deep traceability, or regulated approvals are central. Start with the questions your process must answer Before selecting software, make sure the team can answer these questions for each requirement: What is the requirement, and where did it come from?

articles.title: What is the difference between a factory reset and flashing stock firmware?
articles.excerpt: A Galaxy phone that is acting up leaves you with two nuclear options. You can factory reset it, or you can flash stock firmware. People often treat them as the same thing, because both end with a phon…
articles.body: A Galaxy phone that is acting up leaves you with two nuclear options. You can factory reset it, or you can flash stock firmware. People often treat them as the same thing, because both end with a phone that looks fresh out of the box. But they work at completely different levels, and picking the wrong one either wastes an afternoon or leaves the real problem untouched. Knowing what each one actually does saves you from both mistakes. A factory reset wipes your data, not your software A factory reset erases everything you added to the phone. Your apps, your photos, your accounts, your settings, and your files are all gone. What remains is the software the phone was already running, exactly as it was before the reset.

articles.excerpt: Most small business websites have a home page that gets all the attention and a set of service pages that were written in an afternoon and never touched again. That's a missed chance. When someone sea…
articles.body: Most small business websites have a home page that gets all the attention and a set of service pages that were written in an afternoon and never touched again. That's a missed chance. When someone searches for "website development in Ranchi" or "accounting software for shops", Google usually wants to show them a page about that one service, not your home page. A good service page does two jobs: it tells Google clearly what you offer and where, and it convinces the person who lands there to get in touch. Here's how I approach both. One service, one page The most common mistake I see is a single "Services" page listing everything in short bullet points. It's tidy, but it gives Google very little to work with, and it gives a visitor no reason to trust you.

articles.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
articles.excerpt: Fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a Finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on Nov. 21.
articles.body: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA launches Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day.

articles.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
articles.excerpt: For over a century astronomers have speculated that comets could have delivered organic molecules necessary for life to Earth, but new modeling shows these molecules wouldn't have survived impact.
articles.body: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

articles.title: OpenAI is sunsetting ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice next month
articles.excerpt: OpenAI is going all in on GPT-Live.
articles.body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR OpenAI has announced that it will retire ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice on December 11, 2026. The company is focusing on unifying the voice experience through GPT-Live. Live video and screen sharing will continue to use Advanced voice until GPT-Live has this capability. Earlier this year, OpenAI rolled out a new voice model called GPT-Live . The Gemini Live rival joined ChatGPT Advanced and Standard voice as yet another way to have more natural conversations with the chatbot. As the saying goes, three is a crowd, and OpenAI is ready to do some streamlining. OpenAI has announced that a big change is coming for ChatGPT Voice. On December 11, 2026, the company will be retiring Advanced and Standard voice.
